content: Ohio University, located in Athens, Ohio, is a public institution established in 1804, making it the oldest university in Ohio and the first in the Northwest Territory. The university's campus spans 1,800 acres. It was originally founded as the American Western University, following the Northwest Ordinance of 1800, which emphasized the importance of education for governance and societal well-being. The first students enrolled in 1808, and the university awarded its first bachelor's degrees in 1815. Over the years, Ohio University has developed a reputation for excellence in various fields, including journalism, visual communication, and avionics engineering. The E.W. Scripps School of Journalism, established with funding from the Scripps Foundation, is one of the university's most distinguished programs. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs in areas such as advertising management, broadcast news, magazine journalism, and public relations. The school has been consistently ranked among the top journalism programs in the nation. In 1975, Ohio University founded the College of Osteopathic Medicine, which remains the only osteopathic medical school in Ohio. The university is also home to the Avionics Engineering Center, a leading research facility specializing in electronic navigation, communication, and surveillance systems. This center, part of the Russ College of Engineering and Technology, has been instrumental in addressing challenges in air transportation. The John Calhoun Baker Center, a state-of-the-art student center, opened in 2007. Designed with Georgian-style architecture and modern interiors, the six-story facility includes a food court, fine dining restaurant, ballroom, coffee shop, theater, and computer labs. Its innovative design, featuring escalators that connect different levels of the campus, has been recognized as a best practice in student center planning. Ohio University is organized into several colleges, including the College of Arts & Sciences, College of Business, Scripps College of Communication, Russ College of Engineering and Technology, and the College of Fine Arts. It also operates five regional campuses in Eastern (St. Clairsville), Zanesville, Lancaster, Southern (Ironton), and Chillicothe, serving over 8,000 students. The university has been classified as a Doctoral/High Research Activity institution by the Carnegie Foundation, reflecting its robust graduate programs and research initiatives. Its libraries house over 2.4 million bound volumes. Ohio University students have achieved significant success in securing nationally competitive awards, including Fulbright Scholarships, the Truman Scholarship, and the Goldwater Scholarship. Research at Ohio University is supported by numerous centers and institutes across disciplines. These include the Institute for Sustainable Energy and the Environment, the Edison Biotechnology Institute, the Appalachian Rural Health Institute, and the Nanoscale and Quantum Phenomena Institute. The university also fosters innovation through its business incubator, the Innovation Center. The College of Fine Arts emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach to arts education, with faculty who are both accomplished artists and educators. The Kennedy Museum of Art, located in historic Lin Hall, houses notable collections, including Native American textiles and contemporary prints. The School of Recreation and Sport Sciences offers nationally recognized programs in athletic training, exercise physiology, and sports administration. Its Sport Management Program is one of the few in the country accredited by the Sport Management Program Review Council. The Russ College of Engineering and Technology, named after alumnus Dr. Fritz J. Russ, provides undergraduate and graduate programs in traditional engineering fields. It is home to approximately 1,400 undergraduates and 300 graduate students. Ohio University's athletic teams, known as the Bobcats, compete in NCAA Division I as part of the Mid-American Conference. The football program, established in 1894, has a storied history, including five MAC Football Championships and a National Small College Championship in 1960. The men's basketball program has also achieved significant success, with multiple NCAA Tournament appearances and a Pre-Season National Invitation Tournament victory in 1994. Other successful sports programs include volleyball, swimming and diving, wrestling, and baseball. The university's athletic facilities, such as Peden Stadium and the Convocation Center, are among the best in the conference. The Marching 110, Ohio University's marching band, is renowned for its high-energy performances and has performed at prestigious events, including Carnegie Hall and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. Ohio University operates a network of public radio and television stations under the umbrella of Ohio University Public Media. WOUB Public Media broadcasts PBS programming and student-produced content, including the nightly news program Newswatch. The university also supports student-run media, such as ACRN.com, an internet-only radio station, and The Post, an independent campus newspaper. The university boasts a distinguished list of alumni, including Roger Ailes, founder of Fox News; Richard Dean Anderson, actor; Nancy Cartwright, voice of Bart Simpson; Clarence Page, Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist; and Mike Schmidt, Hall of Fame baseball player. Other notable alumni include Arsenio Hall, comedian and talk show host; Piper Perabo, actress; and George Voinovich, former U.S. Senator and Ohio governor.
